outline.name: PMI Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline 2026
outline.version: July 2026 PMP Certification Exam Update; document footer reads 'revised 11 August 2026'. Domains: People 33%, Process 41%, Business Environment 26%; about 40% predictive and 60% agile or hybrid items.
outline.notes: 26 tasks (ECO.P1 to ECO.B8) and 138 enablers (ECO.<task>.e<n>, numbered in the ECO's printed order: People 39, Process 64, Business Environment 35). PMI numbers tasks within each domain (Task 1..N); the P/R/B codes follow engine.js TASKNAMES, where R = Domain II Process and B = Domain III Business Environment. All text is paraphrased; no ECO or PMBOK text is copied. PMI says enablers are illustrative, not exhaustive. Every enabler maps only to its parent task. The ECO does not name Kanban, flow, WIP limits, or cumulative flow; per course rule they are placed in match lists where the ECO's wording points to them: R3 (prioritize by value, deliver incrementally: Kanban, pull system, flow), R8 (schedule by approach and executing it: Kanban, continuous flow, WIP limits, cadence, cycle time, lead time, throughput; variance via cumulative flow, burndown), R9 (metrics and artifacts: cumulative flow diagrams, Kanban board, velocity, cycle time), B4 (impediments: WIP limits, bottlenecks, blocked items, swarming). New 2026 themes the ECO names explicitly: sustainability (R1.e3, R7.e5, B2.e1, B5.e6) and AI only in the introduction (AI tools added to R1.e9 match as a data-for-decisions example). Some enabler match lists include short acronyms (EV, PV, AC, CV, SV, CPI, SPI, RBS) which can over-match; reviewers may want to tighten them. Reviewer adjustment 2026-11-07: the "WIP limits?" phrase widened to also accept "limit WIP" and "limit on work in progress" (same concept, word order only).
